{"abstract":"We register a formally specified and machine-checked kernel for a federated automated adjudication system in which independent computational lines judge mathematical and operational claims. The kernel comprises: (i) a three-rung, three-track credibility lattice obtained as the free completion of a legacy five-element poset, verified by exhaustive enumeration over all 11^3=1331 ordered triples and fully re-formalized in Lean 4 (fourteen theorems by decision over the finite carrier); (ii) a five-state certificate lifecycle machine with nine legal transitions and machine-checked invariants, also re-formalized in Lean 4 -- the formalization caught a specification flaw in one invariant, which we report; (iii) certified numerical anchors: uniqueness of the gauged fixed point of circulant entropic-optimal-transport (Sinkhorn) systems, established by a Krawczyk interval operator with outward rounding across a six-instance family (k in {6,10}, epsilon in {1,1/2,1/5}), and ported to the Lean 4 verified interval library leancert; (iv) a parameterized Lean 4 template for Rice-type undecidability, with an instantiation generator and three discharged instances; and (v) a minimal trusted computing base result: the soundness of an interval certificate checker (accept implies correctness), itself machine-proved. All Lean artifacts were verified on cloud infrastructure (Axiom Axle, environment lean-4.28.0) with axiom audits restricted to propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
